components.css: .ds-section-row { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(136px, 1fr)); align-items: stretch; gap: 10px; } .ds-section-card { min-width: 0; border: 1px solid #e7e7ea; border-radius: 10px; background: #f6f6f7; overflow: hidden; } .ds-section-card.is-active { border-color: #91a3da; background: #fff; box-shadow: inset 0 -2px 0 #5068b7; } .ds-section-card button { width: 100%; height: 100%; min-height: 84px; padding: 13px; border: 0; background: transparent; align-items: start; text-align: left; } .ds-section-card small { max-height: none; overflow: visible; } .ds-section-stage { margin-top: 12px; min-height: 120px; padding: 22px; border-radius: 12px; background: #f6f6f7; box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px #e7e7ea; } @media (max-width: 700px) { .ds-section-row { grid-template-columns: repeat(2, minmax(0, 1fr)); } } @media (max-width: 430px) { .ds-section-row { grid-template-columns: 1fr; } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-section-card, .ds-section-stage { transition: none; } }

narrative.overview: GoalBoard is a high-frequency workbench, not a dashboard. Its visual system makes one selected Goal continuous across a cool-gray Project and Goal navigator, an independent Hero above a separate Focus work surface, and a Runtime whose application chrome follows GoalBoard while the terminal canvas has an independent palette. The design is quiet because the frame is structural: sibling surfaces use only faint lines and breathing room, shadows are absent, and hierarchy comes from typography, stable selectors, alignment, and whitespace.
keyCharacteristics: Continuous desktop regions with separate inset Goal Hero and work surfaces.
Cool monochrome surfaces with a restrained cobalt focus color.
Goal overview organized as a primary work column and a compact supporting context rail.
One reusable stationary selector row and shared detail stage across Context, Progress, Relationships, and Record.
Compact information density in navigation, with calm reading density in the selected Goal.
Runtime application chrome follows GoalBoard; only the terminal canvas becomes a distinct execution environment.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Cobalt appears only for focus, links, progress, and selected intent. It never becomes a decorative field or a general-purpose card tint.

rules.name: The Semantic Color Rule
rules.body: Green, amber, and red always describe real application state and appear with text, never as decoration.

rules.name: The Bounded State Rule
rules.body: Every Goal state is an icon-and-text tag with a semantic border and quiet tint; it never relies on color alone or becomes an unbounded word at the edge of a row.

rules.name: The Native Clarity Rule
rules.body: Do not introduce display fonts or monospace styling for atmosphere. Monospace remains limited to commands, identifiers, and measured values.

rules.name: The Continuous Region Rule
rules.body: Navigator, Goal canvas, and Runtime remain structural regions. Goal Hero and work content are sibling inset surfaces separated by visible canvas space; neither uses a drop shadow or nested ornamental frame. Compact may tighten vertical rhythm but keeps at least 18px of horizontal safety inside overview cards.

rules.name: The One Active Section Rule
rules.body: Each Focus detail tab exposes one stable equal-width selector row and one shared full-width detail stage. Selection never moves sibling cards; deep links reveal the owning stage before scrolling.

rules.name: The Content Before Controls Rule
rules.body: Project utilities fit inside the title row and Goal actions use short stable labels; layout never concedes a row or a content column to dynamic button copy.

rules.name: The Runtime Boundary Rule
rules.body: Goal ownership, tabs, guidance, child choices, and controls are application UI. Only the real terminal canvas uses terminal colors, selected locally as Follow interface, Light, or Dark.

rules.name: The Transient Elevation Rule
rules.body: If a surface remains on screen as part of the workspace, it stays flat. Only content temporarily placed above the workspace may cast a shadow.

dos: Do establish hierarchy with proportion, alignment, and whitespace before adding a container.
Do keep one selected Goal visually continuous across Navigator, Focus, and Runtime.
Do preserve the cool-neutral palette and reserve cobalt for interaction and focus.
Do test Light, Dark, Standard, Compact, Runtime-open, narrow states, and both terminal palettes together.
Do keep every mobile workspace surface full width and free of horizontal viewport escapes.
Do let users scan section summaries before expanding one body, and reveal the correct card before honoring a deep link.
donts: Don't reintroduce a centered brand ornament, a floating Goal paper card, or large rounded persistent panes.
Don't turn detail tabs, view switches, and every filter into segmented pills.
Don't stack unrelated detail sections into one unbroken page or give every nested content block another decorative border.
Don't make status colors decorative or rely on color without text.
Don't copy YouMind's product IA, content cards, branding, or imagery.
